heading: About
name: Swayam
main_text: I build the invisible parts of software — APIs, deployment platforms, sandboxes, and detection pipelines — and I treat security as a design constraint, not a feature bolted on at the end.
sub_text: I'm pursuing two degrees in parallel: a B.Tech in Cybersecurity at VIT Vellore and a BS in Data Science at IIT Madras. That mix shapes how I engineer — every system should be observable, measurable, and hard to break. Recent work includes a Kubernetes-native deployment platform (Kargo), a multi-tenant quality layer for MCP servers (PlugFit), a Linux sandboxing engine built on NsJail (Sandboxd), and a Windows SIEM pipeline with custom detection rules. Off the keyboard-shipping path, I reverse engineer binaries, dig into system internals, and tune detection logic for fun.
security_principles: Security is an invariant, not a feature.
Observability is a prerequisite for security.
Simplicity is the ultimate hardening tool.

principle_proofs.text: In Tributary, API keys are hashed and closed by default, and a leaked key can trash files but never delete them permanently.
